name: Spicy Asian Veggie Ground, Bok Choy & Snap Pea Stir-Fry over Rice
ingredients: 8 fl oz chicken or vegetable broth
instructions: Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a medium saucepan. Add water and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.

Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
While the rice cooks, place broth, chili-garlic sauce, soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, and cornstarch in a small bowl; whisk to combine the sauce and set aside.
Trim and cut bok choy crosswise into 1-inch strips. Place in a large bowl.
Halve snap peas crosswise and add to the bowl with the bok choy; set aside.
Preheat a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add veggie ground and cook, breaking it apart with a spoon, until browned and crumbly, 4-5 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel and mince ginger and garlic. Add both to the bowl with the veggies.
Trim green onions and cut crosswise into ¼-inch pieces; add half to the bowl. (Reserve remaining green onions for serving.)
When the veggie ground is done, add veggies, ginger, garlic, salt, and pepper to the skillet; stir-fry until veggies soften, about 3 minutes.
Add sauce to the skillet and continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens, 2-3 minutes more. Remove from heat.
To serve, divide rice and stir-fry between plates; sprinkle with reserved green onion and enjoy!
author: Mealime
